results.title: Patch Tuesday - Wikipedia
results.content:
Microsoft formalized Patch Tuesday in October 2003.
Microsoft introduced "Patch Tuesday" in October 2003 to reduce the cost of distributing patches after the Blaster worm.
This system accumulates security patches over a month, and dispatches them all on the second Tuesday of each month, an event for which system administrators may prepare.
↑ "April 2020 Patch Tuesday: Microsoft fixes three actively exploited vulnerabilities".

results.title: Microsoft’s biggest-ever Patch Tuesday fixes 206 bugs, including 3 zero-days | Malwarebytes
results.content:
Microsoft’s biggest-ever Patch Tuesday fixes 206 bugs, including 3 zero-days
This month’s Patch Tuesday fixes 206 security flaws in Microsoft software, making it the biggest Patch Tuesday release ever.
The update includes 32 critical vulnerabilities, as well as three publicly disclosed zero-days.
The huge number of fixed vulnerabilities makes this the largest Patch Tuesday since Microsoft launched the program in October 2003.

results.title: Update release cycle for Windows clients | Microsoft Learn
results.content:
The monthly security update release is published on the second Tuesday of each month, typically at 10:00 AM Pacific Time (PST/PDT).
The release includes both new and previously released security fixes, along with nonsecurity content introduced in the prior month's Optional nonsecurity preview release.
Optional nonsecurity preview releases are typically released on the fourth Tuesday of the month at 10:00 AM Pacific Time (PST/PDT).
